title: Runtime contract gating and staged-change playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: codify a pragmatic, operational playbook for making compatibility-sensitive changes to the serving runtime. Focus areas: (1) clear change classification and contract-level gates, (2) automated canary/cascading rollout with measurable SLO gates (latency, p99, errors, token throughput, KV-cache hit rate), (3) upgrade assistant tooling to produce consumer migration plans, and (4) emergency rollback/compat fallback policies. This ticket produces an actionable playbook + CI checks + a minimal CLI tool for producing migration reports and gating metadata attached to releases.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Change classifier defined (breaking | soft-deprec | additive) with examples and mapping to semver bump rules.
A2: Canary gating thresholds documented and enforced by CI for runtime releases (latency p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, error rate).
A3: Release artifact contains machine-readable 'compat-manifest' used by upgrade-assistant and by the console to inform customers about migration actions.

A4: Upgrade-assistant CLI can: (a) ingest compat-manifest, (b) run lightweight regression prompts against guarded prompt-set, (c) emit per-route risk scores and suggested rollout plan (canary % steps, time windows).
A5: Playbook includes emergency rollback steps, impact communication template, and a postmortem checklist for compatibility regressions.
implementation_plan: Step 1: Draft change classifier matrix and semver mapping with concrete examples (target: 1 week).
Step 2: Define telemetry signals and thresholds for gating (SLOs + dashboards). Instrument a canary pipeline in CI to run perf + correctness harness on each release candidate.

Step 3: Implement 'compat-manifest' schema (JSON lines) and add to release artifacts. Make schema intentionally minimal but extensible: changed-endpoints, binary-layout, kv-cache-format, deprecation-notes.
Step 4: Build upgrade-assistant prototype (CLI + lightweight runner) that executes canary plan and outputs human-readable plan + machine-readable checklist.
Step 5: Run internal dogfood: upgrade 2 non-critical internal services via the playbook; capture metrics and iterate.
Step 6: Roll out enforcement: CI block on missing compat-manifest for changes classified as 'breaking' or 'soft-deprec'.

risks_tradeoffs: Risk: Overly conservative gates increase release latency and slow feature delivery. Tradeoff: allow 'opt-in' experimental flags with explicit support windows.
Risk: Too permissive classification leads to customer regressions. Tradeoff: invest engineering time in automated regression harness and representative prompt sampling.
Risk: Strict binary/kv compatibility rules may block performance optimizations. Tradeoff: provide automatic conversion tools and a short-term compatibility shim layer for older clients.
Operational note: Emergency rollback must include state reconciliation steps for KV cache and model-version pinned consumer configs to avoid split-brain during partial rollbacks.
